title: SLO drift playbook and sparse-span coverage remediation for console observability
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: During a capacity-driven incident on 2025-02-04 the Console experienced intermittent tenant-level SLO regressions. Root cause analysis identified multiple observability blind spots that slowed diagnosis and delayed mitigation: missing aggregate queue-depth metrics for the ingress router, sparse span sampling for long-tail KV cache evictions, and several dashboards that did not surface tenant-level heatmaps for tail latency. These gaps meant on-call and engineers were unable to quickly determine whether regressions were tenant-specific, capacity-related, or caused by model kernel scheduling changes.

Goal: Create a repeatable playbook and implement instrumentation + dashboard changes to reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR) for future capacity/regression incidents. Deliverables include: 1) a runbook for SLO drift incidents, 2) new metrics and sampling rules for tracing, 3) tenant-level tail-latency heatmaps on the Console, and 4) a small detector that flags sudden drops in per-tenant KV cache hit-rate and queue depth anomalies.
action_items: Add aggregate queue_depth gauge to ingress-router (actor: Diego) — expose per-tenant and global aggregations with 1s granularity
Increase trace sampling rate for eviction and kv-cache related spans from 0.1% to 2% for burst windows and enable slow-path sampling for requests > 200ms (actor: Observability infra)
Create Console dashboard tiles: per-tenant tail latency heatmap, per-tenant kv-cache hit/miss ratio, ingress queue depth over time (actor: Console UX)
Implement an alert: tenant_queue_depth_ratio > 0.8 sustained for 30s => PagerDuty SRE (actor: SRE)
Publish SLO Drift Playbook (Confluence) with triage checklist and decision tree; link runbook to incident postmortem (actor: Aisha)
Backfill missing historical metrics where possible and add migration notes for telemetry consumers (actor: Observability infra)
Write e2e smoke test to validate queue_depth metric propagation and dashboard rendering in staging (actor: QA)
Schedule 2-hour tabletop run through playbook during next oncall rotation and capture feedback (actor: Eng Leads)
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Initial RCA session completed. Confirmed missing aggregate queue_depth in ingress-router; sampling config review scheduled.
2025-02-17: Prototype queue_depth metric instrumented in feature branch (github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/PR#1284). ETA for merge: 2025-02-21.
2025-02-21: PR#1284 merged after perf bench. Added dashboard widget schema; Console UX to wire tile during 2025-W09.
2025-02-25: Tracing sampling proposal approved by Observability SIG. Implemented adaptive sampling in dev; PR#342 (github.com/redwood-inference/observability/PR#342) opened.
2025-03-01: Playbook draft published (confluence.internal.redwood.ai/display/OBS/SLO+Drift+Playbook) and invited SRE and Console leads for review.
2025-03-05: QA smoke test scaffolded and failing intermittently due to metric aggregation lag — Observability infra investigating aggregation flush interval.
2025-03-05: Tablet session scheduled for 2025-03-18 to walk through runbook and alerting thresholds.
decisions: Adopt per-tenant aggregation keys for queue_depth to avoid high-cardinality histograms; keep global agg as a separate series.
Use adaptive trace sampling triggered by latency and eviction event rate instead of uniformly increasing baseline sample rate.
Expose tenant heatmaps only for customers with > 1k requests/day to limit dashboard cost and noise; provide an opt-in flag for enterprise tenants.
Alerting threshold chosen: queue_depth_ratio > 0.8 sustained for 30s to balance false positives and early detection.
